target: Malam ini saya ingin makan nasi goreng spesial pakai telur.
english: Tonight I want to eat special fried rice with an egg.
grammar: Pakai adds toppings when ordering: pakai telur = with an egg.

target: Rendang daging di rumah makan Padang itu empuk sekali.
english: The beef rendang at that Padang restaurant is really tender.

target: Tadi kami memesan dua porsi sate kambing di warung sebelah.
english: Earlier we ordered two portions of goat satay at the warung next door.

target: Gado-gado itu sayuran rebus dengan bumbu kacang yang gurih.
english: Gado-gado is boiled vegetables with savory peanut sauce.
grammar: Gurih = savory-rich (coconut milk, broth, fried things) — a core taste word with no exact English match.

target: Bakso di sini kuahnya bening dan dagingnya kenyal.
english: The bakso here has clear broth and springy meatballs.

target: Soto ayam biasanya disajikan dengan nasi putih dan kerupuk.
english: Chicken soto is usually served with white rice and crackers.

target: Saya lebih suka soto Lamongan daripada soto Betawi yang pakai santan.
english: I prefer Lamongan soto to Betawi soto, which uses coconut milk.

target: Warung nasi campur dekat pasar itu selalu ramai waktu jam makan siang.
english: That mixed-rice warung near the market is always busy at lunchtime.

target: Ayam bakarnya manis karena diolesi kecap sebelum dibakar.
english: The grilled chicken is sweet because it is brushed with kecap before grilling.
grammar: Kecap = soy sauce (kecap manis = sweet), not ketchup — English borrowed the word from Malay.

target: Kalau ke Yogyakarta, kamu harus mencoba gudeg yang manis itu.
english: If you go to Yogyakarta, you have to try that sweet gudeg.

target: Mie ayam di depan sekolah itu murah dan porsinya besar.
english: The chicken noodles in front of that school are cheap and the portions are big.

target: Saya pesan sate ayam sepuluh tusuk, bumbu kacangnya dipisah, ya.
english: I'll have ten skewers of chicken satay, with the peanut sauce separate, please.
grammar: Sate is counted in tusuk (skewers): sepuluh tusuk = ten skewers.

target: Nasi gorengnya pakai ayam atau udang, Kak?
english: Does the fried rice come with chicken or shrimp, miss?

target: Gulai kambing di sini kuahnya kental dan bumbunya terasa kuat.
english: The goat gulai here has thick broth and the spices really come through.

target: Pecel lele biasanya dijual di tenda kaki lima waktu malam.
english: Fried catfish pecel is usually sold at roadside tents at night.
grammar: Kaki lima = street vendors, named after the five-foot walkway (kaki lima) they occupy.

target: Setiap pagi ibu membeli lontong sayur dari penjual keliling.
english: Every morning Mom buys lontong sayur from a roving vendor.

target: Nasi uduk dengan telur balado cocok sekali untuk sarapan.
english: Nasi uduk with balado egg is just right for breakfast.

target: Saya belum pernah mencoba rawon, sup daging dengan kuah hitam itu.
english: I have never tried rawon, that beef soup with black broth.

target: Es cendol paling enak diminum siang hari waktu panas.
english: Iced cendol is most delicious drunk at midday when it is hot.

target: Martabak manis dengan keju dan cokelat itu makanan favorit anak saya.
english: Sweet martabak with cheese and chocolate is my child's favorite food.

target: Sambal di warung itu pedasnya bukan main.
english: The sambal at that warung is unbelievably spicy.
grammar: Bukan main = 'no joke', unbelievably: pedasnya bukan main = it is seriously spicy.

target: Kuah sotonya gurih karena pakai kaldu ayam asli.
english: The soto broth is savory because it uses real chicken stock.

target: Ikan asin goreng cocok dimakan dengan nasi hangat dan sambal.
english: Fried salted fish goes well with warm rice and sambal.

target: Kopi tanpa gula terasa pahit, tapi saya sudah terbiasa.
english: Coffee without sugar tastes bitter, but I am already used to it.
grammar: Ter- + biasa = terbiasa (used to it): sudah terbiasa = already used to it.

target: Sayur pare memang pahit, tapi banyak orang menyukainya.
english: Bitter gourd really is bitter, but many people like it.

target: Mangga muda rasanya asam, jadi biasanya dimakan dengan bumbu rujak.
english: Young mango tastes sour, so it is usually eaten with rujak seasoning.

target: Sup buatan saya kemarin hambar karena kurang garam.
english: The soup I made yesterday was bland because it lacked salt.
grammar: Hambar = bland. The fix is garam (salt): kurang garam = not enough salt.

target: Menurut ayah, tehnya kurang manis, jadi dia menambah gula.
english: According to Dad, the tea is not sweet enough, so he adds more sugar.

target: Rasa asam dari jeruk nipis membuat soto ini lebih segar.
english: The sour taste from the lime makes this soto fresher.

target: Masakan Padang terkenal gurih karena banyak memakai santan kental.
english: Padang cooking is famously savory because it uses a lot of thick coconut milk.

target: Keripik singkong ini asin dan renyah, cocok untuk teman minum teh.
english: These cassava chips are salty and crunchy, perfect to go with tea.

target: Jangan merebus sayur terlalu lama supaya tidak lembek.
english: Don't boil the vegetables too long so they don't go mushy.

target: Tahu goreng ini garing di luar dan lembut di dalam.
english: This fried tofu is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.
grammar: Garing and renyah both mean crispy: garing for fried-dry crunch, renyah for fresh crunch.

target: Dagingnya direbus dulu berjam-jam sampai benar-benar empuk.
english: The meat is boiled for hours first until it is really tender.
grammar: Empuk = tender, soft to the bite: dagingnya empuk = the meat is tender.

target: Kerupuk cepat melempem kalau tidak disimpan di toples tertutup.
english: Crackers quickly go soggy if they are not kept in a closed jar.

target: Sate yang dibakar terlalu lama jadi keras dan kering.
english: Satay that is grilled too long turns tough and dry.

target: Telur setengah matang enak dimakan dengan roti bakar.
english: Soft-boiled eggs are tasty eaten with toast.
grammar: Setengah matang = half-cooked: soft-boiled eggs, rare steak. Matang = cooked/ripe.

target: Pisang gorengnya masih panas, renyah sekali di luar.
english: The fried bananas are still hot, really crispy on the outside.

target: Nasinya sudah matang, ayo kita makan sekarang.
english: The rice is done — come on, let's eat now.

target: Di rumah kami, ikan lebih sering dikukus daripada digoreng.
english: At our house, fish is steamed more often than fried.
grammar: Cooking talk loves di- passives: dikukus = steamed, digoreng = fried, direbus = boiled.

target: Dapur langsung wangi waktu ibu menumis bumbu halus.
english: The kitchen instantly smells fragrant when Mom sautés the spice paste.

target: Ayah lebih suka ikan bakar, sedangkan saya suka ikan goreng.
english: Dad prefers grilled fish, while I like fried fish.
grammar: Sedangkan contrasts two subjects: ayah suka A, sedangkan saya suka B = Dad likes A, while I like B.

target: Sisa rendang semalam dipanaskan lagi untuk makan siang hari ini.
english: Last night's leftover rendang is reheated for lunch today.

target: Tempe goreng buatan ibu selalu habis duluan di meja makan.
english: Mom's fried tempeh is always the first thing gone from the dinner table.

target: Sayur asem buatan nenek rasanya segar dan sedikit asam.
english: Grandma's sayur asem tastes fresh and slightly sour.

target: Ibu selalu mencicipi masakannya dulu sebelum disajikan ke meja.
english: Mom always tastes her cooking first before it is served at the table.

target: Kalau masak untuk banyak orang, bumbunya harus ditambah sedikit demi sedikit.
english: When cooking for many people, the seasoning has to be added little by little.
grammar: Sedikit demi sedikit = little by little; demi repeats units: satu demi satu = one by one.

target: Ayam kampung memang lebih mahal, tapi rasanya lebih gurih.
english: Free-range chicken really is more expensive, but it tastes richer.
grammar: Ayam kampung (lit. village chicken) = free-range chicken — pricier and tastier than broiler.

target: Nasi sisa kemarin digoreng dengan bawang putih dan kecap.
english: Yesterday's leftover rice is fried with garlic and kecap.

target: Ikan kecil ini digoreng kering supaya durinya ikut renyah.
english: These small fish are fried until dry so even the bones turn crispy.

target: Sebelum dibakar, ayamnya direbus dulu supaya cepat matang.
english: Before being grilled, the chicken is boiled first so it cooks quickly.

target: Lontong dibuat dari nasi yang dimasak di dalam daun pisang.
english: Lontong is made from rice cooked inside a banana leaf.

target: Kata ibu, sup bening cocok untuk anak yang sedang sakit.
english: Mom says clear soup is right for a child who is sick.

target: Kami jarang menggoreng di rumah karena dapur jadi penuh asap.
english: We rarely deep-fry at home because the kitchen gets full of smoke.

target: Akhir pekan depan kami mau membakar ikan di halaman belakang.
english: Next weekend we want to grill fish in the backyard.
grammar: Grilling is bakar, never masak: membakar ikan = to grill fish. Masak = cooking in general.

target: Mas, nasi gorengnya pedasnya level berapa, ya?
english: Excuse me, what spice level is the fried rice?
grammar: -nya makes a quality the topic: pedasnya level berapa? = how spicy is it (its spiciness, what level)?

target: Saya minta level dua saja, saya tidak kuat pedas.
english: I'll take level two please — I can't handle spice.
grammar: Tidak kuat + noun = can't handle it: saya tidak kuat pedas = I can't take spice.

target: Teman saya kuat makan pedas, level lima pun masih kurang.
english: My friend can handle spicy food — even level five is not enough.
grammar: Pun after a word = even: level lima pun masih kurang = even level five is not enough.

target: Kalau tidak tahan pedas, jangan pesan ayam geprek di sini.
english: If you can't stand spice, don't order the ayam geprek here.

target: Sambalnya boleh dipisah supaya anak-anak juga bisa makan?
english: Can the sambal be separate so the kids can eat too?

target: Pedasnya baru terasa setelah suapan ketiga.
english: The heat only hits after the third bite.

target: Mukanya langsung merah karena sambal hijau Padang itu pedas sekali.
english: His face immediately turns red because that Padang green sambal is really spicy.

target: Minum es teh manis membantu kalau mulut terasa terbakar.
english: Drinking sweet iced tea helps when your mouth feels like it is burning.

target: Orang sini biasa makan sambal sejak kecil, jadi lidahnya kuat.
english: People here are used to eating sambal from childhood, so their tongues are tough.

target: Makan di sini atau dibungkus, Kak?
english: For here or to go, miss?
grammar: The warung question: makan di sini atau dibungkus? = for here or to go? Bungkus = wrap up, take away.

target: Bungkus dua nasi campur, ya, sambalnya jangan lupa.
english: Two mixed rice to go, please — don't forget the sambal.

target: Di warung Tegal, kamu tinggal tunjuk lauk yang kamu mau.
english: At a Tegal warung, you just point at the side dishes you want.
grammar: Warteg (warung Tegal) = cheap point-and-choose rice stalls named after the town of Tegal.

target: Air putih di warung biasanya gratis, tinggal minta saja.
english: Plain water at a warung is usually free — you just have to ask.

target: Pembeli boleh mengambil sendiri kerupuk dari toples di meja.
english: Customers may take crackers themselves from the jars on the table.

target: Bayarnya nanti saja di kasir setelah selesai makan.
english: You pay later at the register, after you finish eating.
grammar: Warung habit: eat first, pay after — bayarnya nanti saja = just pay later.

target: Warung ini ramai terus karena masakannya seperti masakan rumah.
english: This warung is always busy because its food is like home cooking.

target: Sarapan bubur ayam di gerobak depan gang sudah jadi kebiasaan saya.
english: Chicken porridge at the cart in front of the alley has become my breakfast habit.

target: Tukang sate lewat depan rumah hampir setiap malam.
english: The satay seller passes in front of the house almost every night.
grammar: Tukang + food = the seller: tukang sate = satay man, tukang bakso pushes his cart around.

target: Kalau kamu mendengar suara ketukan kayu, itu tanda tukang bakso lewat.
english: If you hear the sound of wood knocking, that is a sign the bakso seller is passing.

target: Gorengan hangat paling laku waktu sore hujan seperti ini.
english: Warm fried snacks sell best on a rainy afternoon like this.
grammar: Gorengan = the family of street fried snacks: tempe, tahu, bakwan, pisang goreng.

target: Soto Anda nasinya dicampur atau dipisah, Pak?
english: Would you like the rice mixed into your soto or separate, sir?

target: Waktu hujan begini, paling enak makan bakso yang kuahnya panas.
english: In rain like this, nothing beats bakso with hot broth.

target: Untuk minumnya, saya pesan es jeruk tanpa gula.
english: For the drink, I'll order iced orange juice without sugar.

target: Boleh minta sendok dan garpu lagi? Sendok saya jatuh.
english: May I have another spoon and fork? My spoon fell.

target: Pesanan kami kurang satu, sate kambingnya belum datang.
english: Our order is one short — the goat satay has not arrived yet.

target: Maaf, saya tidak makan daging sapi, ada menu ayam atau ikan?
english: Sorry, I don't eat beef — is there a chicken or fish dish?

target: Masakan ini pakai kacang tidak? Anak saya alergi kacang.
english: Does this dish use peanuts? My child is allergic to peanuts.

target: Saya vegetarian, jadi saya pesan gado-gado tanpa telur.
english: I'm vegetarian, so I'll order gado-gado without egg.

target: Tolong nasinya setengah porsi saja, saya tidak terlalu lapar.
english: Just half a portion of rice, please — I'm not very hungry.

target: Rendangnya tinggal dua potong, mau saya ambilkan dua-duanya?
english: There are only two pieces of rendang left — shall I get you both?
grammar: -kan can mean doing it for someone: ambilkan = fetch (for you).

target: Kalau sotonya kurang asin, tambahkan garam sendiri di meja.
english: If the soto is not salty enough, add salt yourself at the table.

target: Menu hari ini ayam goreng lengkuas dan sayur lodeh.
english: Today's menu is galangal fried chicken and lodeh vegetable stew.

target: Soto ayamnya ditambah perasan jeruk nipis supaya lebih segar.
english: The chicken soto gets a squeeze of lime added so it is fresher.

target: Jangan lupa aduk kopinya dulu, gulanya masih di bawah.
english: Don't forget to stir the coffee first — the sugar is still at the bottom.

target: Bakwan jagung paling enak dimakan selagi masih panas.
english: Corn fritters are most delicious eaten while they are still hot.
grammar: Selagi = while it lasts: selagi masih panas = while it is still hot.

target: Anak saya baru mau makan sayur kalau dicampur ke nasi goreng.
english: My child will only eat vegetables if they are mixed into fried rice.
grammar: Baru here = only then: baru mau makan = will only eat (once the condition is met).

target: Suami saya yang masak setiap akhir pekan, saya bagian cuci piring.
english: My husband is the one who cooks every weekend; I'm on dish duty.
grammar: Saya bagian X = X is my department: saya bagian cuci piring = I handle the dishes.

target: Kami menanam cabai di pot supaya tidak perlu sering membeli.
english: We grow chilies in pots so we don't have to buy them often.

target: Resep soto ini turun-temurun dari nenek buyut kami.
english: This soto recipe has been handed down from our great-grandmother.
grammar: Turun-temurun = handed down through the generations (turun = to descend).

target: Bau rendang dari dapur membuat semua orang cepat lapar.
english: The smell of rendang from the kitchen makes everyone hungry fast.

target: Kalau malas masak, kami tinggal pesan makanan lewat aplikasi.
english: When we don't feel like cooking, we just order food through an app.
grammar: Tinggal + verb = all that's left to do: tinggal pesan = just order.

target: Ibu memisahkan porsi adik dulu sebelum sambalnya dicampur.
english: Mom sets aside my little brother's portion first before the sambal is mixed in.

target: Kulkas kami penuh sisa makanan dari acara keluarga kemarin.
english: Our fridge is full of leftovers from yesterday's family gathering.

target: Setiap Lebaran, dapur rumah nenek penuh dengan panci besar.
english: Every Eid, Grandma's kitchen is full of big pots.

target: Ketupat dan opor ayam hampir selalu ada waktu Lebaran.
english: Ketupat and chicken opor are almost always around at Eid.

target: Totalnya berapa, Bu? Sekalian sama es tehnya.
english: How much is the total, ma'am? Together with the iced tea.
grammar: Sekalian = while we're at it, all together: sekalian sama es tehnya = including the iced tea.

target: Kita bagi dua saja, ya, biar gampang.
english: Let's just split it in two, okay, to keep things easy.
grammar: Biar = casual supaya (so that): biar gampang = so it's easy.

target: Kali ini saya yang bayar, kamu sudah traktir minggu lalu.
english: This time I'm paying — you already treated last week.

target: Jangan rebutan bayar, lebih baik kita bagi rata saja.
english: Don't fight over paying — better we just split it evenly.
grammar: Bagi rata = split evenly (rata = flat, even): kita bagi rata = we split it equally.

target: Makanannya kita bayar masing-masing, minumnya biar saya.
english: We each pay for our own food; leave the drinks to me.

target: Uangnya kurang lima ribu, nanti saya ganti setelah ke ATM.
english: I'm five thousand short — I'll pay you back after going to the ATM.

target: Saya sudah jadi langganan warung itu sejak pindah ke sini.
english: I've been a regular at that warung since moving here.

target: Minta bonnya dipisah, ya, soalnya ini pakai uang kantor.
english: Please split the bill — this one is on office money.

target: Kemarin kami mengumpulkan uang bersama untuk makan malam perpisahan tim.
english: Yesterday we pooled money together for the team's farewell dinner.
grammar: Pooling money is patungan — among friends you'll hear: patungan, yuk! = let's chip in!

target: Siapa yang belum bayar? Masih kurang dua puluh ribu.
english: Who has not paid yet? We're still twenty thousand short.

target: Porsi bungkus nasi Padang biasanya lebih banyak daripada makan di tempat.
english: A takeaway portion of nasi Padang is usually bigger than eating in.
grammar: Porsi bungkus = takeaway portion; Padang stalls famously give extra rice when you bungkus.

target: Sate kambingnya masih setengah matang, tolong dibakar sebentar lagi.
english: The goat satay is still half-cooked — please grill it a little longer.

target: Kuah bakso di warung itu gurihnya beda dari yang lain.
english: The bakso broth at that warung has a savoriness unlike the others.

target: Di pasar malam kemarin, kami mencoba kerak telor untuk pertama kali.
english: At the night market yesterday, we tried kerak telor for the first time.

target: Sehabis berenang, paling enak minum es kelapa muda di pinggir pantai.
english: After swimming, nothing beats drinking iced young coconut by the beach.

target: Ayam gorengnya masih panas, hati-hati waktu menggigitnya.
english: The fried chicken is still hot — careful when biting into it.

target: Saya kurang suka pete, tapi suami saya doyan sekali.
english: I don't much like stink beans, but my husband loves them.
grammar: Doyan = really into a food (casual): doyan pedas = loves spicy food.

target: Durian itu baunya kuat, ada yang suka, ada yang tidak tahan.
english: Durian has a strong smell — some people love it, some can't stand it.
grammar: Ada yang ... ada yang ... = some ... others ...: ada yang suka, ada yang tidak = some do, some don't.

target: Teh di sini otomatis manis, kalau mau tanpa gula, minta teh tawar.
english: Tea here is automatically sweet — if you want it sugarless, ask for teh tawar.
grammar: Tawar = plain, unsweetened (and also 'to bargain'): teh tawar = unsweetened tea.

target: Setiap daerah di Indonesia punya soto dengan rasa yang berbeda.
english: Every region in Indonesia has soto with a different flavor.

target: Bumbu kacang gado-gado di sini diulek langsung di depan pembeli.
english: The gado-gado peanut sauce here is ground fresh right in front of the customer.
grammar: Diulek = ground on a stone mortar (ulekan) — what gives sambal its rough texture.

target: Perut saya sudah kenyang, tapi es campur ini menggoda sekali.
english: My stomach is already full, but this es campur is so tempting.

target: Setelah makan pedas, jangan langsung minum air dingin banyak-banyak.
english: After eating spicy food, don't immediately drink lots of cold water.

target: Oleh-oleh paling aman dibawa pulang itu keripik dan sambal botol.
english: The safest souvenirs to bring home are chips and bottled sambal.

target: Kalau kamu ke Solo, jangan lupa mencoba nasi liwet di sana.
english: If you go to Solo, don't forget to try nasi liwet there.
